title: Meet M, N and O
goal: Recognise, name and write M, N, O.
cue: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.
spelling: A letter has a name. Later, we will learn the sounds it can represent in words. Today, say the letter names.

dialogue.name: Kore
dialogue.text: Do these two shapes have the same name?

task: Point to M and O. Say their names, then write their lowercase partners.
story: The letter M has a big form and a small form.

cards.title: Letter M

articulation.label: Letter M
articulation.alt: Letter M: /ɛ/ → /m/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /ɛ/: Front tongue; open the jaw a little more.
/m/: Close both lips; air goes through the nose.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.

articulation.label: Letter O
articulation.alt: Letter O: /oʊ/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /o/: Start with a mid-back tongue and round lips.
/ʊ/: Raise the back tongue a little more.
articulation.note: Keep each vowel glide inside one syllable.

cards.title: Five words to hear and use
sections: the large natural object seen in the night sky. The moon is bright tonight.
A home that a bird makes for its eggs. The bird is in its nest.
a round citrus fruit with thick orange skin. Puck buys two oranges.
an adult male person. A woman and a man are by the door.
the part of your face used for smelling. Touch your nose with one finger.
Listen to each word. Point or act to show its meaning. Say one word, then one short sentence. Ask for help with spelling patterns you have not learned yet.
